subject: general
question: Which of the following idioms means ‘going to sleep’?

options.text: Keep an ear to the ground

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Hit the sack"** means going to sleep. (सोने जाना)

 
 
• **Example: **After a long day at work, I am ready to **hit the sack..**
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. Hit the sack**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Break new grounds** (नया रास्ता बनाना): Doing something innovative or pioneering.

 
 
• **Example:** The researchers are breaking new grounds in cancer treatment.
 
 
 
• **Keep an ear to the ground** (सतर्क रहना): Stay informed or be aware of recent developments.
 
 
• **Example:** It's important to keep an ear to the ground in the tech industry.
 
 
 
• **Run around in circles** (बेकार में समय गवाना): Be very active but not achieve anything.
 
 
• **Example:** Without a clear plan, we’ll just run around in circles.
 
 

46:Taf2,

The correct answer is: **Option 1.**
